result:
All done — `bash tests/run_tests.sh` passes all 8 tests (6 original + 2 new).

**What was changed:**

- **`rotate.sh`** — bug 1: `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"`, which keeps only the *oldest* keep−1 entries and always deletes the newest (and with `total -lt keep` as the only early exit, `total == keep` fell through and deleted exactly one archive — the newest). Now it exits early when `total -le keep` and deletes the oldest `total - keep` entries via `head -n "$((total - keep))"`. Option parsing and `resolve_dir` now come from `lib/common.sh`.
- **`verify.sh`** — bug 2: `awk '{print $2}'` truncated sidecar file names at the first space, so `my backup-….tar.gz` looked "archive missing" → BAD/exit 2. Now `read -r expected file <<< "$line"` keeps the whole name (the digest is still field 1, so space-containing names work). Also quoted the digest comparison. Option parsing and `resolve_dir` now come from `lib/common.sh`.
- **`lib/common.sh`** (new) — the shared option-parsing block (verbatim from the scripts) plus `resolve_dir`, with a double-sourcing guard like `lib/log.sh`; scripts must define `usage` and `parse_local_option` before sourcing it, which both do. All flags (`--dest`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q`, `-n`, `-h`, local-option dispatch) behave unchanged.
- **`tests/run_tests.sh`** — added one test per bug: `rotate --keep 3` with exactly 3 archives deletes nothing (all 3 remain, rc=0), and `verify` reports `ok`/rc=0 for an intact archive whose name contains a space.

`backup.sh`, `restore.sh` and `report.sh` were left untouched as requested.
